Hello,

As a debugging expert, I've analyzed the build failure. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Analysis

The build is failing with the error `cd: mfem: No such file or directory`. This error occurs during the compilation step:

```
RUN (cd mfem && make parallel -j$(nproc)) && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=./mfem
```

This indicates that the `mfem` directory, which is a git submodule of the `Laghos` repository, does not exist within the `/opt/laghos` working directory at the time of the build.

The root cause lies in the preceding `RUN` instruction responsible for cloning the repository and its submodules:

```dockerfile
RUN git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git /opt/laghos && \
    cd /opt/laghos && \
    git submodule update --init --recursive
```

While this command chain appears correct, relying on `cd` within a single `RUN` instruction can be fragile inside the Docker build environment. The `git submodule update` command is failing to execute in the correct context, thus the `mfem` submodule is never checked out.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, we should use a more robust and idiomatic approach for cloning a repository with its submodules. The `git clone` command provides a `--recursive` flag that handles this in a single, atomic operation, avoiding any shell-related issues.

I will replace the complex, multi-part `RUN` instruction with a single, reliable `git clone --recursive` command. This ensures the `mfem` submodule is correctly initialized.

Here is the corrected Dockerfile:

```dockerfile
# Specifies the base image. Ubuntu 22.04 LTS is a stable, well-supported choice.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set the default shell to bash for RUN instructions to support advanced scripting.
SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-c"]

# Set a non-interactive frontend for package installations to avoid prompts.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure that MPI communication uses the standard TCP/IP network
# interface (eth0) and avoids attempting to use high-performance interconnects
# (like InfiniBand) or shared-memory mechanisms that may not be available or
# may cause issues in a container.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1

# Install dependencies and fix the system shell for build script compatibility.
# - wget: Added to download build-time dependencies (e.g., hypre) for MFEM.
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure network communication.
# - build-essential, g++, gfortran, make, git: Standard compilation toolchain.
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: Open MPI runtime and development libraries.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    wget \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    # Force /bin/sh to be /bin/bash to ensure build scripts that explicitly call
    # /bin/sh but use bash-specific syntax (e.g., '[[') work correctly.
    rm /bin/sh && ln -s /bin/bash /bin/sh && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone the repository and its submodules using a single, robust command.
# The '--recursive' flag ensures the 'mfem' submodule is cloned automatically.
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git /opt/laghos

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository for the build step.
WORKDIR /opt/laghos

# Build the parallel MFEM dependency and then the parallel Laghos application.
# The MFEM library (a submodule) must be built first. We then build Laghos and
# explicitly provide the correct path to the library via MFEM_DIR.
RUN (cd mfem && make parallel -j$(nproc)) && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=./mfem

# Copy the correctly named parallel 'laghos-p' executable to a system location
# and rename it to 'laghos' so it can be executed directly from the PATH.
RUN cp /opt/laghos/laghos-p /usr/local/bin/laghos

# Set a clean working directory for the application's runtime.
# This is where the application will be executed from.
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the necessary input data files from the source directory to the runtime WORKDIR.
# These files are required by Laghos to run its simulations.
RUN cp /opt/laghos/data/* .

# Clean up the build environment to create a smaller, more secure final image.
# This step removes the source code and all build tools that are not needed at runtime.
RUN apt-get purge -y --auto-remove \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /opt/laghos /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# The image is now ready. The entrypoint and command should be specified
# at runtime, for example, in a Kubernetes Job manifest, to allow for
# flexibility in running different simulations.
# Example command: mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 1 -m cube01_hex.mesh -rs 3 -tf 0.75
```

ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1

# - ca-certificates: Required for secure network communication (e.g., git clone over https).
# - build-essential, g++, gfortran, make: Standard toolchain for compiling C, C++, and Fortran code.
# - git: For cloning the application source code from its repository.
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: Open MPI runtime and development libraries.

# The package list cache is cleaned up in the same layer to reduce final image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone the Laghos source code from its official repository.
# --recursive is used to clone all necessary submodules, such as MFEM.
# The code is placed in /opt/laghos to keep it separate from the final runtime environment.
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git /opt/laghos

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository for the build step.
WORKDIR /opt/laghos

# Build the parallel version of the Laghos executable.
# The Laghos makefile is configured to build the MFEM dependency automatically.
# -j$(nproc) utilizes all available CPU cores to speed up the compilation process.
RUN make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled 'laghos' executable to a standard system location (/usr/local/bin)
# so it can be executed directly without specifying its full path.
RUN cp /opt/laghos/laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos

# Set a clean working directory for the application's runtime.
# This is where the application will be executed from.
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the necessary input data files from the source directory to the runtime WORKDIR.
# These files are required by Laghos to run its simulations.

# no longer needed at runtime. It also clears the apt cache again.

    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \

As a debugging expert, I've analyzed the build failure. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Analysis

The build is failing with the error `cd: mfem: No such file or directory`. This error occurs during the compilation step:

```
RUN (cd mfem && make parallel -j$(nproc)) && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=./mfem
```

This indicates that the `mfem` directory, which is a git submodule of the `Laghos` repository, does not exist within the `/opt/laghos` working directory at the time of the build.

The root cause lies in the preceding `RUN` instruction responsible for cloning the repository and its submodules:

```dockerfile
RUN git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git /opt/laghos && \
    cd /opt/laghos && \
    git submodule update --init --recursive
```

While this command chain appears correct, relying on `cd` within a single `RUN` instruction can be fragile inside the Docker build environment. The `git submodule update` command is failing to execute in the correct context, thus the `mfem` submodule is never checked out.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, we should use a more robust and idiomatic approach for cloning a repository with its submodules. The `git clone` command provides a `--recursive` flag that handles this in a single, atomic operation, avoiding any shell-related issues.

I will replace the complex, multi-part `RUN` instruction with a single, reliable `git clone --recursive` command. This ensures the `mfem` submodule is correctly initialized.

# Set a non-interactive frontend for package installations to avoid prompts.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure that MPI communication uses the standard TCP/IP network
# interface (eth0) and avoids attempting to use high-performance interconnects
# (like InfiniBand) or shared-memory mechanisms that may not be available or
# may cause issues in a container.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1

# Install build dependencies, runtime dependencies, and necessary tools.
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure network communication (e.g., git clone over https).
# - build-essential, g++, gfortran, make: Standard toolchain for compiling C, C++, and Fortran code.
# - git: For cloning the application source code from its repository.
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: Open MPI runtime and development libraries.
# --no-install-recommends is used to minimize image size.
# The package list cache is cleaned up in the same layer to reduce final image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# FIX: Clone the specific 'master' branch to ensure submodules are correctly initialized.
# --recursive is used to clone all necessary submodules, such as MFEM.
# The code is placed in /opt/laghos to keep it separate from the final runtime environment.
RUN git clone --branch master --recursive https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git /opt/laghos

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository for the build step.
WORKDIR /opt/laghos

# Build the MFEM submodule first, as it is a dependency for Laghos.
# Then, build the parallel version of the Laghos executable.
# -j$(nproc) utilizes all available CPU cores to speed up the compilation process for both steps.
RUN make -C mfem parallel -j$(nproc) && make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled 'laghos' executable to a standard system location (/usr/local/bin)
# so it can be executed directly without specifying its full path.
RUN cp /opt/laghos/laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos

# Set a clean working directory for the application's runtime.
# This is where the application will be executed from.
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the necessary input data files from the source directory to the runtime WORKDIR.
# These files are required by Laghos to run its simulations.
RUN cp /opt/laghos/data/* .

# Clean up the build environment to create a smaller, more secure final image.
# This step removes the source code, build tools, and development libraries that are
# no longer needed at runtime. It also clears the apt cache again.
RUN apt-get purge -y --auto-remove \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /opt/laghos /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# The image is now ready. The entrypoint and command should be specified
# at runtime, for example, in a Kubernetes Job manifest, to allow for
# flexibility in running different simulations.
# Example command: mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 1 -m cube01_hex.mesh -rs 3 -tf 0.75

### Error Analysis

The build is failing with the error `cd: mfem: No such file or directory`. This error occurs during the compilation step:

```
RUN (cd mfem && make parallel -j$(nproc)) && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=./mfem
```

This indicates that the `mfem` directory, which is a git submodule of the `Laghos` repository, does not exist within the `/opt/laghos` working directory at the time of the build.

The root cause lies in the preceding `RUN` instruction responsible for cloning the repository and its submodules:

```dockerfile
RUN git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git /opt/laghos && \
    cd /opt/laghos && \
    git submodule update --init --recursive
```

While this command chain appears correct, relying on `cd` within a single `RUN` instruction can be fragile inside the Docker build environment. The `git submodule update` command is failing to execute in the correct context, thus the `mfem` submodule is never checked out.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, we should use a more robust and idiomatic approach for cloning a repository with its submodules. The `git clone` command provides a `--recursive` flag that handles this in a single, atomic operation, avoiding any shell-related issues.

I will replace the complex, multi-part `RUN` instruction with a single, reliable `git clone --recursive` command. This ensures the `mfem` submodule is correctly initialized.

FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set the default shell to bash for RUN instructions to support advanced scripting.
# The default /bin/sh (dash) does not support syntax like '[[' used by dependencies.
SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-c"]

# Set a non-interactive frontend for package installations to avoid prompts.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure that MPI communication uses the standard TCP/IP network
# interface (eth0) and avoids attempting to use high-performance interconnects
# (like InfiniBand) or shared-memory mechanisms that may not be available or
# may cause issues in a container.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1

# Install dependencies and fix the system shell for build script compatibility.
# - wget: Needed by the MFEM build system to download its own dependencies.
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure network communication (git, wget).
# - build-essential, g++, gfortran, make, git: Standard compilation toolchain.
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: Open MPI runtime and development libraries.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    wget \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    # Force /bin/sh to be /bin/bash to ensure build scripts that explicitly call
    # /bin/sh but use bash-specific syntax work correctly.
    rm /bin/sh && ln -s /bin/bash /bin/sh && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone the latest (default) branch of the repository and explicitly initialize its submodules.
# This is a more robust method to ensure the mfem dependency is available for the build step.
RUN git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git /opt/laghos && \
    cd /opt/laghos && \
    git submodule update --init --recursive

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository for the build step.
WORKDIR /opt/laghos

# Build the parallel MFEM dependency and then the parallel Laghos application.
# The MFEM library (a submodule) must be built first. We then build Laghos and
# explicitly provide the correct path to the library via MFEM_DIR.
# -j$(nproc) utilizes all available CPU cores to speed up compilation.
RUN (cd mfem && make parallel -j$(nproc)) && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=./mfem

# Copy the compiled parallel executable ('laghos-p') to a system location
# and rename it to 'laghos' so it can be executed directly from the PATH.
RUN cp /opt/laghos/laghos-p /usr/local/bin/laghos

# Set a clean working directory for the application's runtime.
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the necessary input data files from the source directory to the runtime WORKDIR.
# These files are required by Laghos to run its simulations.
RUN cp /opt/laghos/data/* .

# Clean up the build environment to create a smaller, more secure final image.
# This step removes the source code and all build tools that are not needed at runtime.
RUN apt-get purge -y --auto-remove \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /opt/laghos /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# The image is now ready. The entrypoint and command should be specified
# at runtime, for example, in a Kubernetes Job manifest, to allow for
# flexibility in running different simulations.
# Example command: mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 1 -m cube01_hex.mesh -rs 3 -tf 0.75

# Set a non-interactive frontend for package installations to avoid prompts.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings ensure that MPI communication uses the standard TCP/IP network
# interface (eth0) and avoids attempting to use high-performance interconnects
# (like InfiniBand) or shared-memory mechanisms that may not be available or
# may cause issues in a container.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1

# Install build dependencies, runtime dependencies, and necessary tools.
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure network communication (e.g., git clone over https).
# - build-essential, g++, gfortran, make: Standard toolchain for compiling C, C++, and Fortran code.
# - git: For cloning the application source code from its repository.
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: Open MPI runtime and development libraries.
# --no-install-recommends is used to minimize image size.
# The package list cache is cleaned up in the same layer to reduce final image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone the Laghos source code from its official repository.
# --recursive is used to clone all necessary submodules, such as MFEM.
# The code is placed in /opt/laghos to keep it separate from the final runtime environment.
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git /opt/laghos

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository for the build step.
WORKDIR /opt/laghos

# Build the parallel version of the Laghos executable.
# The Laghos makefile is configured to build the MFEM dependency automatically.
# -j$(nproc) utilizes all available CPU cores to speed up the compilation process.
RUN make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled 'laghos' executable to a standard system location (/usr/local/bin)
# so it can be executed directly without specifying its full path.
RUN cp /opt/laghos/laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos

# Set a clean working directory for the application's runtime.
# This is where the application will be executed from.
WORKDIR /app

# Copy the necessary input data files from the source directory to the runtime WORKDIR.
# These files are required by Laghos to run its simulations.
RUN cp /opt/laghos/data/* .

# Clean up the build environment to create a smaller, more secure final image.
# This step removes the source code, build tools, and development libraries that are
# no longer needed at runtime. It also clears the apt cache again.
RUN apt-get purge -y --auto-remove \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /opt/laghos /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# The image is now ready. The entrypoint and command should be specified
# at runtime, for example, in a Kubernetes Job manifest, to allow for
# flexibility in running different simulations.
# Example command: mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 1 -m data/cube01_hex.mesh -rs 3 -tf 0.75

Hello,

As a debugging expert, I've analyzed the build failure. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Analysis

The build is failing with the error `cd: mfem: No such file or directory`. This error occurs during the compilation step:

```
RUN (cd mfem && make parallel -j$(nproc)) && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=./mfem
```

This indicates that the `mfem` directory, which is a git submodule of the `Laghos` repository, does not exist within the `/opt/laghos` working directory at the time of the build.

The root cause lies in the preceding `RUN` instruction responsible for cloning the repository and its submodules:

```dockerfile
RUN git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git /opt/laghos && \
    cd /opt/laghos && \
    git submodule update --init --recursive
```

While this command chain appears correct, relying on `cd` within a single `RUN` instruction can be fragile inside the Docker build environment. The `git submodule update` command is failing to execute in the correct context, thus the `mfem` submodule is never checked out.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, we should use a more robust and idiomatic approach for cloning a repository with its submodules. The `git clone` command provides a `--recursive` flag that handles this in a single, atomic operation, avoiding any shell-related issues.

I will replace the complex, multi-part `RUN` instruction with a single, reliable `git clone --recursive` command. This ensures the `mfem` submodule is correctly initialized.

Hello,

As a debugging expert, I've analyzed the build failure. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Analysis

The build is failing with the error `cd: mfem: No such file or directory`. This error occurs during the compilation step:

```
RUN (cd mfem && make parallel -j$(nproc)) && make p -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=./mfem
```

This indicates that the `mfem` directory, which is a git submodule of the `Laghos` repository, does not exist within the `/opt/laghos` working directory at the time of the build.

The root cause lies in the preceding `RUN` instruction responsible for cloning the repository and its submodules:

```dockerfile
RUN git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git /opt/laghos && \
    cd /opt/laghos && \
    git submodule update --init --recursive
```

While this command chain appears correct, relying on `cd` within a single `RUN` instruction can be fragile inside the Docker build environment. The `git submodule update` command is failing to execute in the correct context, thus the `mfem` submodule is never checked out.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, we should use a more robust and idiomatic approach for cloning a repository with its submodules. The `git clone` command provides a `--recursive` flag that handles this in a single, atomic operation, avoiding any shell-related issues.
